items.title: Best Hermes Agent Memory: Every Provider Compared (2026)
items.content:
The best Hermes Agent memory setup for most people is Hermes’s built-in memory plus a plain-text vault like Obsidian — then one memory provider if you need more. In the video below I show Hermes, Jarvis-style voice and Obsidian memory working together. Here’s how Hermes memory works, every provider compared, and what I’d choose.

Key takeaways

Built-in memory (MEMORY.md and USER.md) is always on.
Hermes supports nine external memory providers; only one can be active.
Honcho models you; Hindsight builds a knowledge graph.
Three providers leave core on 15 October 2026 — install them from the catalogue.






How Hermes Agent memory works
Out of the box, Hermes keeps two memory files — MEMORY.md for what it learns and USER.md for what it knows about you — and nudges itself to save useful facts. It can also search past sessions with full-text search and summarise what it finds. An external provider adds to this; it doesn’t replace it.

My pick for the best Hermes Agent memory

Everyone: built-in memory plus an Obsidian vault Hermes can read and write.
Personal assistant use: add Honcho, which models your preferences over time.
Research and knowledge work: add Hindsight for knowledge-graph memory.
Fully local and private: Holographic or ByteRover — from the catalogue once they leave core.

Why a plain-text vault matters
Memory providers are great, but your most valuable knowledge should live in files you own. I keep mine in an Obsidian vault that every agent in my Agent OS can read, so nothing is locked inside one tool. If you ever switch providers, or agents, the vault comes with you.
Keep Hermes memory clean

Review MEMORY.md and USER.md every week.
Delete wrong or outdated facts.
Use separate profiles or bots for separate jobs, so memories don’t blur.
Don’t store passwords or keys in memory.

My Hermes memory management routine takes 15 minutes a week.

Most people should run built-in memory for a few weeks before adding a provider — you’ll know exactly what’s missing.
What changes on 15 October 2026
The Hermes docs say Holographic, RetainDB and ByteRover are scheduled to leave core on 15 October 2026. If you use one, check the docs after that date for how to keep using it, likely through the plugin catalogue like Honcho, Mem0 and the others.
How memory makes Hermes better over time
Memory is what turns Hermes from a clever chatbot into an assistant that knows you. It remembers your business, your audience, your style rules and the mistakes you’ve corrected, so every task starts from where the last one finished. Combined with skills, that compounding effect is huge: after a few weeks you stop re-explaining yourself and start getting work that fits first time. That’s why keeping memory accurate and well organised is one of the highest-value habits you can build with any AI agent.
There’s a privacy side too. Built-in memory and a local vault keep everything on your machine. Cloud providers can be more powerful, but they mean your memories live on someone else’s servers. Decide what you’re comfortable with before you install a provider, and keep anything sensitive out of memory entirely. For most people, a local-first setup with a well-organised vault gives you the best balance of power and privacy.
Finally, give it time. Memory gets more valuable the longer you use Hermes, so judge it after a month of real work, not after a single afternoon. By then you’ll see exactly where it helps and where a provider would add something worthwhile.
How I’d get started this week
Open MEMORY.md and USER.md today and read what Hermes has saved. Fix anything wrong, delete anything stale, and add three facts you want it to always know — your business, your audience and your preferred style. Connect an Obsidian vault if you use one. Only then decide whether you need an external provider, and if so, pick the one that matches how you use Hermes.
Memory mistakes to avoid

Never reviewing memory — wrong facts compound.
One profile for everything — research, content and personal memories blur.
Stacking providers — only one external provider can be active.
Saving secrets — keep keys and passwords out of memory.
No backup — keep your vault in a folder that’s backed up.

Avoid those and memory becomes Hermes’s biggest advantage over a normal chatbot.
Memory and voice together
In the video above I combine Hermes memory with a Jarvis-style voice and an Obsidian vault. You talk, Hermes remembers, and the notes land in your vault where every agent can use them. That loop is what makes an agent feel like it actually knows you.
The bottom line on the best Hermes Agent memory
The best Hermes Agent memory is built-in memory, a vault you own, and at most one provider chosen for your use case. Keep it clean and Hermes gets smarter every week.

Nine external providers, and only one can be active at a time alongside built-in memory.

Run hermes plugins install with the provider name, then hermes memory setup.

Built-in memory, Holographic and ByteRover run locally.

No — built-in memory and session search persist across sessions.

items.title: Best Hermes Agent Tools: The Built-In Tools Worth Using (2026)
items.content:
The best Hermes Agent tools are the ones that let it actually do things: the browser tools, the terminal, sub-agent delegation and cron jobs. Hermes ships with 60+ built-in tools, and in the video below I show it controlling a computer. Here’s every tool that matters, the toolsets that group them, and how to switch them on and off.

Key takeaways

Hermes has 60+ built-in tools, grouped into toolsets.
My top four: browser, terminal, delegate_task and cronjob.
Run hermes tools to configure tools per platform.
Add more tools with MCP servers and plugins.






Best Hermes Agent tools: the built-ins




Tool
What it does




web_search, web_extract
Search the web and pull clean text from pages


browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_vision
Drive a real browser and see the page


terminal, process
Run commands and background jobs


read_file, write_file, patch
Work with files


execute_code
Run code in a sandbox


delegate_task
Spin up sub-agents for parallel work


cronjob
Schedule recurring jobs


memory, session_search
Remember facts and search past sessions


vision_analyze, image_generate, text_to_speech
See images, make images, speak


x_search
Search X/Twitter (off by default)


MCP and plugin tools
Anything you connect, e.g. Home Assistant




My top 4 Hermes Agent tools
1. The browser tools. Hermes can navigate, read and see real web pages, which unlocks research and web tasks on any site.
2. The terminal. It runs commands locally or in Docker, SSH, Daytona, Singularity, Modal or Vercel Sandbox, so you can sandbox anything risky.
3. delegate_task. Hermes spins up sub-agents to work in parallel — big research jobs finish far faster.
4. cronjob. Schedule anything and have the results delivered to any platform. This is what turns Hermes from a chatbot into an employee.

Want this working in your business, not just bookmarked? Getting real work done with Hermes Agent tools is exactly what we build together inside the AI Profit Boardroom — 3,400+ members, four live calls a week, and a full one-hour DeepSeek Harness course in the classroom.
Prefer it mapped 1-on-1 first? Book a free strategy session and we’ll plan it for your exact situation.

Hermes Agent toolsets
Tools are grouped into toolsets, including web, search, terminal, file, browser, vision, image_gen, skills, tts, todo, memory, session_search, cronjob, code_execution, delegation, clarify, messaging and safe. You can enable specific toolsets for a session:
hermes chat --toolsets "web,terminal"
Run hermes tools to see every tool and configure which are available on each platform — for example, a narrower set on Telegram than in your terminal.
Adding more tools to Hermes

MCP servers — connect any MCP server and its tools appear as their own toolset.
Plugins — like Home Assistant for smart-home control. See my best Hermes plugins.
Nous Portal tools — paid subscribers can use web, image generation and more through the Tool Gateway.

Use Hermes tools safely

Use the safe toolset when testing new skills.
Run the terminal in Docker for anything risky.
Give each platform only the tools it needs.
Keep approvals on for sending and deleting.

Hermes terminal backends




Backend
Best for




Local
Your own machine


Docker
Sandboxing commands safely


SSH
Running on another server


Daytona, Modal, Vercel Sandbox
Cloud sandboxes


Singularity
HPC environments




If you’re unsure, use Docker: commands run in a container, so a mistake can’t touch the rest of your system.
Tools that pair with messaging
Hermes connects to 20+ messaging platforms, and the messaging toolset lets it send results there. Combine cronjob, web_search and messaging and you have a daily research assistant that reports to your phone — no extra software needed.
Why tools are what make Hermes an agent
A chatbot can only answer. An agent can act — and tools are how it acts. With search and browser tools Hermes can research anything on the web; with the terminal and file tools it can build and change things on a computer; with delegation it can split a big job across sub-agents; and with cron it can do all of that on a schedule without you. Understanding which tools are switched on, and on which platforms, is the difference between an agent that feels limited and one that feels like a real member of your team. Spend ten minutes in hermes tools and you’ll get far more out of every model you use.
The best part is that you don’t need to memorise any tool names to use them. You describe the job in plain English and Hermes chooses the tools. Your role is simply to make sure the right ones are available, the risky ones are sandboxed, and the results land where you’ll see them. Get that right and every new model you plug in becomes more capable straight away.
As new models launch, revisit your tool settings too. A stronger model can handle more tools at once and chain them into longer tasks, so it’s worth switching on more as your setup matures. Start narrow, prove it works, then widen the toolset step by step as your trust in the agent grows.
How I’d get started this week
Run hermes tools and look at what’s switched on for each platform. Turn off anything you don’t use, make sure browser, terminal, delegation and cron are on where you need them, and switch the terminal to Docker if you’re running anything risky. Then give Hermes one task that uses three tools together — research, write a file, schedule a follow-up — and watch how much it can do.
Tools by job




Job
Tools to switch on




Research
web_search, web_extract, browser


Coding
terminal, file, code_execution


Big projects
delegate_task, todo


Automation
cronjob, messaging


Content
image_generate, text_to_speech, vision


Remembering
memory, session_search




Giving Hermes only the tools a job needs makes it faster, cheaper and safer.
Common tool problems

A tool isn’t available — check it’s enabled for that platform in hermes tools.
Image generation fails — it may need a provider or a Nous Portal subscription.
x_search does nothing — it’s off by default.
Browser tasks are slow — that’s normal; use web_extract when you just need text.

The bottom line on the best Hermes Agent tools
The best Hermes Agent tools are the browser, terminal, delegation and cron — switch them on, sandbox the risky ones, and add MCP servers for anything else you need.

60+ built-in tools, including web search, a browser, terminal, file tools, code execution, sub-agents, cron, memory, vision, image generation and text-to-speech.

Run hermes tools to configure them per platform, or pass –toolsets to hermes chat.

Yes — through its terminal and browser tools, and computer-use features in Hermes Desktop.
Can I add my own tools to Hermes?
Yes — with MCP servers and plugins.

The cronjob tool, because it makes your other tools run on a schedule.

Why run Hermes on a VPS
On a laptop, long-running loops, background browser work and scheduled jobs all compete with everything else — and stop when you close the lid. On a VPS, Hermes gets its own machine that never sleeps, so your 6am brief actually arrives at 6am.

My rule of thumb: the cheapest plan is fine for chat and scheduled research; go up a tier if you use the browser tools heavily or run several agents at once. You only need a big GPU server if you want to run local models on it.
How to install Hermes on a VPS
On any Linux VPS, the official one-line installer works:
curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
Then run hermes setup to connect a model and a messaging platform like Telegram, so you can talk to it from your phone. My Hostinger install guide walks through it step by step.

Use Tailscale instead of exposing ports to the internet.
Keep approvals on for anything that sends or deletes.
Use Docker as the terminal backend to sandbox commands.
Store API keys in Hermes’s config, never in chat.

Is a VPS worth it?
If you only chat with Hermes while you’re at your desk, you don’t need a VPS. The moment you rely on scheduled jobs — a morning brief, inbox triage, weekly reports — or long tasks that run for hours, a VPS pays for itself in reliability. Your laptop stops being a single point of failure, your agent keeps working while you travel or sleep, and you can access it from anywhere through your phone. For the price of a couple of coffees a month, that’s one of the best upgrades you can make to a Hermes setup.
It also opens up more ambitious work. With Hermes on a server you can run big research jobs that split across several sub-agents, keep a browser session working through a long task, or run several bots for different parts of your business at once — none of which you’d want competing with video calls on your laptop. Start small with one scheduled job, and you’ll quickly find more work worth moving to the VPS.
And if you ever outgrow it, moving is simple: your skills, memory files and configuration are just files, so you can copy them to a bigger server or a new provider in minutes. That portability is another reason I prefer running Hermes on infrastructure I control.

If you’ve never run a server, start with Hermes Cloud today and move one scheduled job there. Either way, move your most important daily job first, check it runs reliably for a week, then move the rest.

Opening ports to the internet — use Tailscale instead.
Running as root without a sandbox — use Docker for the terminal.
No messaging platform — you won’t see what your agent is doing.
Never updating — Hermes ships fixes often.
Paying for a GPU server you don’t need — cloud models run elsewhere.
